payload.final_answer: ```python # Background: QR factorization using Householder reflections transforms an m x n matrix A into an upper triangular matrix R by applying a sequence of orthogonal transformations. For each column k from 0 to n-1, a Householder vector v is constructed such that the transformation H = I - 2(vv^T)/(v^Tv) zeros out the elements below the diagonal in the k-th column. The matrix A is updated iteratively as A = H_k * A. The resulting matrix A will have the upper triangular matrix R stored in its upper triangle. import numpy as np def householder(A): '''Inputs: A : Matrix of size m*n, m>=n Outputs: A : Matrix of size m*n (upper triangular part contains R) ''' m, n = A.shape A = A.astype(float) for k in range(n): # Vector x is the part of the column below the diagonal x = A[k:, k] # Construct the Householder vector v norm_x = np.linalg.norm(x) rho = -np.sign(x[0]) if x[0] != 0 else -1 u1 = x[0] - rho * norm_x v = x / u1 v[0] = 1.0 # Beta factor for the reflection beta = -rho * u1 / norm_x # Apply the transformation to the remaining submatrix # A[k:, k:] = (I - beta * v * v^T) * A[k:, k:] A[k:, k:] -= beta * np.outer(v, v.T @ A[k:, k:]) return A ```
